=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md: line 20 (the step 2 "Context" bullet, post-PR state) | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: The step-2 wording unconditionally runs the §26.G sweep after a stale-Routine deletion, even when that deletion was denied; the sweep itself performs `delete_trigger` cleanup calls.
  WHY: Further denials can accumulate classifier blocks until an unattended stage stalls at a prompt nobody can answer.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "§26.I now names both sites. agents.md and the changelog fragment's 'Flows covered' row list them too." (PR description, "Findings fixed" table, item 1)
  Expected change site: `agents.md` post-PR cleanup-sites list (the `/implement-plan-claude` parenthesis enumerated at line 1086-1094 of the PR diff hunk for `agents.md`)
  Evidence of absence: The post-PR `agents.md` list — `resume hygiene, step 2 stale-Routine delete, zombie-checker cleanup, re-arm cleanup, rename on opening a PR, hand-back, end-of-project archives, checker prompt` — omits `a failed two-step start`, which the canonical CLAUDE.md §26.I list and the post-PR command Rules bullet (line 422 of `workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md`) both include. The PR description commits agents.md to enumerate the canonical sites alongside §26.I, but agents.md drifts from §26.I in the opposite direction (narrower, not wider). The changelog fragment's "Flows covered" row does carry `two-step start`, so that side of the contract is met; agents.md is not.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "no flow retries a denied cleanup call." (issue #5068 acceptance criterion, restated in the PR description's "Findings fixed" rationale and §26.I's body text)
  Expected change site: `workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md` line 20 (the step 2 "Context" bullet, post-PR state)
  Evidence of absence: The step-2 instruction continues `then run the stale Routine sweep (CLAUDE.md §26.G)` with no gate on whether the per-stage stale-Routine `delete_trigger` was denied; §26.I requires skipping "the rest of that step's cleanup" after a denial, and the §26.G sweep is itself named in §26.I as a cleanup site, so it is part of "the rest of this step's cleanup". The new test `test_command_rules_cover_the_per_stage_delete_and_rename` checks only that the inline §26.I note and the Rules bullet contain the new phrases; it does not assert that the sweep is skipped on the denial branch, so the test does not catch this runtime failure.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
